HOW_IT_ENDED_-_MEASURED_NOT_INFERRED.observed: both of this session's background tasks -- the run and its PID poll -- were reported stopped at the same moment, and the scope died at 12:03:43Z

the_mechanism_driven_both_ways.TERM_to_the_PROCESS_GROUP: the scope DIED (probe: ActiveState inactive, no child)
the_mechanism_driven_both_ways.TERM_to_the_launching_shell_alone: the scope SURVIVED (probe: the child sleep kept running)
the_mechanism_driven_both_ways.so: `systemd-run --scope` registers processes the CALLER forks, so the run sits in the launching shell's process group and a group-level stop takes it down. An 85-minute run must not be a child of a shell anything else may stop

HOW_IT_ENDED_-_MEASURED_NOT_INFERRED.what_this_is_NOT: not a refusal by the runner, not a coordinator stop, not an out-of-memory kill: the cgroup peak was 2.3G against an 8G cap and the declared 4000 MB growth budget never fired

measured_by_my_own_poll.note: rss held ~730-767 MB against a cgroup peak of 2435 MB reached at S1_load; the run was inside the null loop when it ended

the_remedy_is_NOT_APPLIED_HERE: changing the wrapper is a declaration change to THE_ONE_COMMAND and it needs a review and its own GO (R-620). Candidates: `setsid` before the wrapper, or a transient SERVICE (`systemd-run --user --unit=X -p Slice=research.slice`, no `--scope`) which systemd forks itself and which outlives the caller. Either must keep the slice, the MemoryMax, the CPUQuota and the lock so `wrapper_observed()` still measures what rule 20 requires
what_this_record_is: provenance for a REAL-day run that consumed 35 minutes of work and wrote NOTHING. Without it the CPU time is undocumented and a later reader cannot tell a killed run from a run that never happened

what_this_record_is_not.an_economic_reading: NONE. The run was killed inside the null loop; no artifact was written and nothing was read out of the process
